candidates.tagline: 'Zero-failure' security drone crashes and catches fire at World Cup fan zone
candidates.story: NYPD's Skydio X10 drone — marketed by Skydio as providing 'zero-failure security' with 'autonomous patrols at scale' — malfunctioned, fell from the sky, and caught fire near the FIFA World Cup Fan Zone entrance at Brooklyn Bridge Park on June 23, 2026, while thousands of fans were in the area; this is the second time the same NYPD drone model has caught fire.
candidates.why_funny: A 'zero-failure' security drone achieved total failure in the most literal way possible — by crashing and burning right next to the event it was supposed to protect.
candidates.alt: A black Skydio X10 quadcopter drone in flight against a clear blue sky, rotors spinning, seen from a low angle showing all four arms and propellers
candidates.credit: Sgt. Austin Steinborn / U.S. Army (Wikimedia Commons)

candidates.tagline: The futuristic EV that can't charge at home
candidates.story: Hundreds of Tesla Cybertruck owners discovered their trucks' Power Conversion System (PCS) fails and stops home charging entirely — first dropping from 48A to 24A, then nothing — and Tesla is quietly replacing the $1,000+ part case-by-case rather than issuing a recall, while offering free Supercharging as a workaround so owners must drive to a charging station to recharge an EV.
candidates.why_funny: The $80,000 truck designed to power your house through a blackout can't reliably charge itself in your own garage, so Tesla's fix is 'please go to a petrol station instead.'
candidates.alt: A silver angular Tesla Cybertruck Foundation Series electric pickup truck parked on green grass in front of a tree-lined pond, shot from the front-left showing its distinctive stainless steel body panels
